entry.title: What is investing and how do I start? | Money Matters @moneystocker

media:group.media:title: What is investing and how do I start? | Money Matters @moneystocker
media:group.media:description:
The idea of using money you already have to make even more is an attractive prospect. But all the jargon and the amount of risk involved also make it very intimidating.
James Beckett, known as @moneystocker joins Jamilla Blake to tell us all about investing: what it is, why he does it and how easy it is to get started.
He gives us simple definitions of technical terms (such as stocks, shares, bonds and dividends) and takes us through the different ways you can invest your money (such as ISAs, crypto, property and index funds).
He also stresses the importance of setting specific goals and doing your own research – and discusses how best to use AI to do this.
And stick around to see Tom Heath and another quick-fire quiz round!

entry.title: How do AI and cyber threats affect financial stability? | Money Matters

media:group.media:title: How do AI and cyber threats affect financial stability? | Money Matters
media:group.media:description:
We all rely on financial services every day. And part of the Bank of England's job is to make sure that those services continue to work so that you always have access to your money. This often involves, quite literally, imagining the worst things that could happen in the economy and making sure we're prepared for them.
Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, talks to Jamilla Blake about her role as a 'professional catastrophiser' and the work her area does to make sure that financial services can withstand shocks (such as cyberattacks, recessions or wars) and still meet people's needs.
She explains the origins of the 2008 financial crisis, how it led to businesses going bust, greater unemployment, and a loss of faith in the financial system – as well as how the country recovered and the lessons we learned from it.
She also goes into detail about the effects of the coronavirus pandemic and how it was the 'biggest stress test of the system' since the 2008 crash.
And stick around to see Tom Heath return with his quick-fire quiz round!
ℹ️ This video is not financial advice. The views expressed in the podcast are those of the hosts and guests, and not necessarily those of the Bank of England or its committees.

entry.title: Monetary Policy Report Press Conference, 30 July 2026

media:group.media:title: Monetary Policy Report Press Conference, 30 July 2026
media:group.media:description:
Our Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decides what monetary policy action to take. The MPC sets and announces policy eight times a year (roughly once every six weeks).
In this video, the MPC discusses the decisions taken in July 2026 and answers questions from the press.
